units.source: Providers

Providers are added in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Model Providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section of the AI settings, with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Add Model Provider__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Each one lists the models selected for it, which are the ones the chat offers; a provider with no models selected is not offered in the chat.
Cloud providers using API keys__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__OpenRouter__TRILIUM_PH_2__
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: For all the providers, an API key is needed. Note that this is charged separately from the subscription you might already have (e.g. Claude Pro). If that might be a problem, consider using either a subscription provider (see below) or using it externally via MCP.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: Do note that most other LLM providers (e.g. Groq, Mistral, Together) can still be used in Trilium via the OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint (see below).
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: If you are using a proxy or gateway, you can also configure the base URL, otherwise the default will be used.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: For OpenRouter, the models are billed to your OpenRouter credits, and their prices, context windows and the attachments they read come from OpenRouter's own model list:
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Latest__TRILIUM_PH_1__ models that can use tools are selected by default, such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Anthropic: Claude Sonnet Latest__TRILIUM_PH_3__. OpenRouter points each of them at the newest model of its line, so the selection stays current without editing the provider.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: Models that reason have a reasoning effort dropdown in the chat (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Low__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Medium__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__High__TRILIUM_PH_5__).
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Auto Router__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) picks a model for each message. Below each reply, the chat names the model that wrote it, which is also the case when a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Latest__TRILIUM_PH_4__ model was used.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: The cost shown below a reply is what OpenRouter billed for it, rather than an estimate from the listed prices.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: Image generation models and the deferred __TRILIUM_PH_0__batch__TRILIUM_PH_1__ variants are not listed.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: Chat titles are generated with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Anthropic: Claude Haiku Latest__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: Requests are attributed to Trilium on your OpenRouter activity page.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: For Gemini, a chat that doesn't specify a model uses __TRILIUM_PH_0__, and the automatically generated chat titles use __TRILIUM_PH_1__. A model you select explicitly is used as is and isn't affected by these defaults.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: We don't plan to support all cloud providers, even if the library we are using would theoretically support them. Before opening a PR adding support for a different cloud provider, make sure to discuss it over __TRILIUM_PH_0__GitHub Discussions__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: See also the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section to better understand what data is being sent to a cloud provider.
units.context: Providers > Cloud providers using API keys

units.source: Subscription-based providers__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Trilium integrates multiple __TRILIUM_PH_0__Subscription-based providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Claude Code by reusing your CLI.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ GitHub Copilot by reusing your CLI's ACP.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Google Antigravity by downloading and setting up an ACP for Trilium.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ OpenAI Codex by reusing your CLI through an ACP adapter shipped with Trilium.
Local/self-hosted providers__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Local or self-hosted providers are a free alternative which respects your privacy but requires specific hardware.
Trilium directly supports the following local providers:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Ollama
Generally Ollama runs in the background so it should be directly usable in Trilium as long as the models are downloaded (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ LM Studio

The OpenAI-compatible server is __TRILIUM_PH_0__disabled__TRILIUM_PH_1__ by default in LM Studio installations. First download your desired models through the graphical interface, then go to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Settings__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Developer__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and toggle __TRILIUM_PH_6__Developer mode__TRILIUM_PH_7__. On the left there will be a new __TRILIUM_PH_8__Developer__TRILIUM_PH_9__ tab, with a toggle to start it up.
Even for local providers that are not directly supported by Trilium, you can still use a custom endpoint (see below).

When dealing with self-hosted LLM models, depending on the training and the size of the model, the quality of the output may vary. Before __TRILIUM_PH_0__reporting issues__TRILIUM_PH_1__ regarding the quality of the output (e.g. hallucinating tool calls), consider benchmarking the response against a cloud provider (Claude Sonnet is recommended).
Custom endpoints__TRILIUM_PH_0__

If your desired hosted (e.g. Groq, Mistral, Together) or local LLM provider is not listed in Trilium, you can use the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__OpenAI-compatible__TRILIUM_PH_1__ provider from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Custom endpoint__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section.
This allows you to set the base URL to an OpenAI-compatible API, with an optional API key if required by the service.

Enter the base URL exactly as the service documents it, including its version path, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__. Only a bare host such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__ is completed with __TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The endpoint can run on the same machine as Trilium, elsewhere on your local network or on a Tailscale tailnet. Trilium refuses link-local addresses (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and cloud metadata endpoints, which no model server is served on.
For custom endpoints, the pricing of the models is not known so the cost of a conversation will not be displayed; this is especially relevant for hosted providers.
